idiom_name: class named after the computation: fields for receiver, arguments and former locals, one public entry method, private step methods
implementation_notes: Language-neutral form: create a class named after the computation; give it a field for the original receiver when the algorithm needs it and a field for each argument and each former local; copy them in through a constructor (or a named constructor / static factory); move the body into one public entry method (compute/execute/call); replace the original method with a one-line creation and delegation; then decompose the entry method into private step methods, promoting a temporary to a field only when two or more steps share it. Create a fresh instance per invocation and keep every field private to the computation, so the object is a per-call value rather than cached state.
pitfalls: Stopping after the extraction: the pattern pays off only when the compute method is then decomposed into named step methods that share the fields.
Promoting every temporary to a field, which produces a state machine whose step order becomes an undocumented precondition.
Reusing one instance for several invocations; per-invocation state must be created per call.
Widening the host's encapsulation (package-private accessors) to feed the method object instead of passing only the values it actually needs.

Wrong move: pass the entire host because collecting inputs is inconvenient -> the method object reaches through host internals and becomes feature-envy coupling -> instead pass the narrow values or capability interface it actually needs.

Wrong move: expose promoted temporaries for tests or convenience -> callers can violate step ordering and the one-shot invariant -> instead keep fields private and test through the constructor and single entry method.
